contents.title: Quiz Diagnostic 1ere Anglais - Serie 36
contents.subject: Anglais
contents.description: Diagnostic Anglais 1ere : Les prépositions de temps, lieu et mouvement

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The meeting is ___ Friday ___ 3pm.'
'She was born in 1998' and 'She was born on 15th March 1998' are both grammatically correct.
Complète avec la bonne préposition de lieu (in, on, at) : 'The keys are ___ the table. Your bag is ___ the corner. She's waiting ___ the bus stop.'
Choose the correct preposition of movement: 'She walked ___ the bridge to get to the other side of the river.'
In English, we say 'arrive at the airport' but 'arrive in Paris'.
Explique la différence entre 'go to school' et 'go to the school'.
Which sentence uses a preposition of movement correctly?
choices: He ran along the building to escape.
She jumped onto the stage to perform.
He drove past into the city.

questions.question: 'In the morning' and 'on Monday morning' are both correct but use different prepositions.

exercisenotion.notion: Prépositions de temps : at, on, in
exercisenotion.description: AT + heure précise ou moment précis : at 8pm, at noon, at midnight, at the weekend (UK). ON + jours et dates : on Monday, on 5th March, on my birthday. IN + périodes longues : in the morning, in January, in 2020, in the 19th century, in summer. Exceptions : at night, at Christmas, at Easter.

exercisenotion.notion: Prépositions de lieu : at, on, in
exercisenotion.description: IN = à l'intérieur d'un espace fermé ou délimité : in the room, in Paris, in France, in a box. ON = sur une surface : on the table, on the wall, on the floor, on a bus/train/plane. AT = un point précis, une adresse, un lieu d'activité : at the station, at school, at 15 Baker Street, at the top.

TO = direction vers : go to school, travel to France. INTO = mouvement vers l'intérieur : walk into the room. ONTO = mouvement vers une surface : jump onto the table. THROUGH = passage à travers : walk through the forest. ALONG = le long de : walk along the river. ACROSS = traverser : swim across the lake. PAST = passer devant : walk past the shop.
